newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu demands Arafat stop violence.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu demands Arafat stop violence.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu demanded on Friday Palestinian President Yasser Arafat intervene immediately to stop violence engulfing the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem.

"He must personally intervene and stop the incitement -- so it is heard from him," Netanyahu told a news conference in which he accepted no responsibility for a crisis in which 66 Arabs and Jews have been killed.
"I'm telling him also today: our hand is stretched out to you in peace but we cannot agree that parallel to peace there will be an option of violence or war," he said.
Palestinian officials said Arafat's office would issue a statement later in the day in response to Netanyahu's comments at the news conference.
Speaking in strident tones, Netanyahu said he did not consider his internationally criticised decision to open a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem on Tuesday a blunder.

"I make no excuses and am not sorry about the opening of the Western Wall tunnel which has nothing to do with the Temple Mount, does not do harm to the holy places and which expresses our sovereignty in Jerusalem," he said.
Netanyahu repeated his contention that Arafat "cynically" used the tunnel as an excuse to stir up Arab passions against Israel and force his government into peace concessions.
"Remember, this wasn't a spontaneous combustion. This was a deliberate political decision...it wasn't a spontaneous intifada," Netanyahu said.
"We demand the Palestinian Authority commit itself immediately and in the long-term to stop the violence... return to negotiations and continue the peace process."
But the right-wing leader's chief of military intelligence, speaking at the news conference, voiced doubts Arafat had the power to persuade all his police force to cease fire.
"I am not sure about his ability and capability today, at the present time, to control the height of the flames," Major General Moshe Yaalon said.
Asked if he was also referring to shooting by some of the Palestinian security forces," Yaalon replied: "Yes."

With Israeli tanks now deployed in the West Bank, Netanyahu promised to take "whatever means are necessary" to protect his soldiers from attack by Palestinian police armed by Israel under its peace deals with the PLO.
He did not elaborate but framed his remarks with his sombre-looking defence minister and uniformed army chief at his side.

Netanyahu said he would consider an invitation from Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to meet Arafat in Cairo. Arafat has turned down Netanyahu's invitation to a one-to-one summit. Both men met for the first time earlier this month in Gaza.

"There was an invitation from President Mubarak. I did not rule it out. I am prepared to consider it. I don't think the meeting will be the stumbling block. It won't be a problem. There will be a meeting," Netanyahu said.
Palestinians charge Netanyahu has failed to make any progress towards peace, despite his landmark meeting earlier this month with Arafat.

They note that Netanyahu, citing security concerns, has yet to carry out a troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron agreed by the previous Labour-led government and has pledged to expand Jewish settlements.
Netanyahu said the Palestinian self-rule Authority should expect more problems in forging peace with an Israel under his rule.
"Believe me, there are going to be many frustrations in the peace process, many ups and downs, many impasses, many problems -- that's the nature of negotiations."
